long_biography.plain_text:
Ocean conservation is the centre of Dona Bertarelli's public work. As co-chair of the Bertarelli Foundation, she helped redirect an organisation rooted in reproductive-health education towards marine science and protected areas. She later created the Pew Bertarelli Ocean Legacy project with the Pew Charitable Trusts and founded a digital tool that helps managers monitor marine protected areas.

Competitive sailing supplies a distinct second arena. Bertarelli co-founded an international professional offshore sailing team in 2011 and has combined record attempts with environmental education. During a Jules Verne Trophy attempt in 2016, she became the fastest woman to sail around the world. She also helped launch the Sports for Nature Framework, which brings international sporting and environmental bodies together around biodiversity commitments.
